body: Berkshire's 2025 letter (published 2026) is the first signed by Greg Abel as CEO; Buffett remains Chairman. Stated criteria, verbatim bullets: 'Invest in businesses that we thoroughly understand, with durable advantages and long-term economic prospects'; 'Partner with high integrity leaders who understand their customers and act like owners'; 'Avoid businesses that undermine the fabric of society or could jeopardize Berkshire's reputation'; 'Act quickly and concentrate our capital in a few high conviction ideas'; 'Maintain discipline and let compounding unfold.' Opportunities are judged on growth of 'intrinsic value per share over a time horizon measured in perpetuity.' Cash and US Treasuries 'now exceed $370 billion' - 'our dry powder' - and a large cash position 'does not' signal 'a retreat from investing.' 2025 deals: OxyChem (from Occidental) and Bell Laboratories (rodent control: 'easy to understand and always needed' - 'We only wish it had been ten times bigger'). Buybacks only 'below our estimate of intrinsic value, conservatively determined'; no dividend while $1 retained creates >$1 of value. Operating cash flow $46bn in 2025 vs >$40bn five-year average. Candour carried over: Kraft Heinz 'disappointing', Pilot control delay a 'mistake'. Actionable: a ready-made 5-line purchase checklist; patience with cash is a position, not a failure.
title: Greg Abel's first letter (2025): Berkshire's five capital-allocation criteria and the dry-powder doctrine
